provenance: Manual summary of a physical startup-stage profile, host checkpoint tensor comparisons, two serial wrapper startup orders, parsed localhost HTTP objects and retained local logs. Not a signed or statistically powered benchmark.

packages.build: nix build .#qwen38 --no-link --print-out-paths -L --option substituters '' succeeded locally, including the 2m12s device-free installCheck; a remote-builder SSH warning fell back to the local builder.

bottleneck_profile.hardware: Physical Blackhole P150a IDs 0+1, 1x2 mesh, firmware 19.11.0 and KMD 2.10.0
bottleneck_profile.method: One instrumented service-equivalent Python process, identical TTNN/Python environment and revision-named tensor cache. Process launch to the emitted stage:ready; targeted Python method timers are inclusive and nested, not additive. No request ran before readiness.
bottleneck_profile.interpretation: Language backbone construction is still the largest measured constructor. The separately initialized checkpoint-backed CPU reference visual consumes about 4.5 seconds before the still-required TT vision construction; this CPU stage is the optimization target. Instrumentation and host conditions make the absolute profile time incomparable to the prior 35.943s unprofiled startup.

change: Build the existing HF visual tower on torch meta, assign the same pinned checkpoint BF16 parameters, and explicitly restore its one nonpersistent BF16 rotary-frequency buffer. Neither TT vision/device assembly, cache keys, checkpoint contents, GDN equations nor request initialization moves across stage:ready.

host_checkpoint_comparison.method: Each pinned checkpoint loaded with the original full-FP32-constructor/BF16-cast/copy path and with the candidate meta/assign path. Compared all 333 named parameter values and the rotary-frequency buffer with torch.equal; every candidate parameter and buffer was non-meta, and all pinned checkpoint weights were BF16.

physical_comparison.method: Production clef-serve and clef-flash-serve wrappers, serial one process per arm, same existing revision-qualified TT tensor caches and owner-private TT_METAL_CACHE on spacious /datapool. First order baseline then candidate with 13 HTTP requests per process; immediately afterward reverse order candidate then baseline, startup-only. time.perf_counter from subprocess launch to emitted stage:ready. qwen38-p150x2.service inactive and no competing device holder during measurements. Every process exited with UMD close.

clef_27b_p150x2.response_shapes: 132-token short, 1,637-token cross-chunk text, real 32x32 red PNG (201 tokens), four-frame video (168 tokens), changed/restored states and joint noul/ordinal score (232 tokens). First/restored state responses matched inside each process; output_tokens was zero throughout.

clef_flash_9b_p150_id0.response_shapes: The same 132/1,637/201/168/232-token text, image, video and joint-question shapes; first/restored state responses matched inside each process and output_tokens was always zero.

physical_comparison.latency_scope: The first HTTP requests compiled kernels after readiness and reused the same private binary-cache directory in later arms; first-request timings are not a controlled paired comparison. Single warm-request observations cannot establish request acceleration. The reverse-order Flash candidate took 65.719s, with slower model-config/layer phases before visual loading than its 34.216s baseline; the full-process startup speedup is not established for Flash and the 26.419s initial 27B difference is not attributable solely to this approximately 4s host visual change.

limits: The approximately 4s direct host visual-loading reduction is checkpoint- and environment-specific. Instrumented child phases overlap; one startup per package/variant/order is not a latency distribution, and OS page-cache, host contention, mesh setup and other startup phases vary substantially.

No broad accuracy or numerical GDN simulator pass: TTsim still lacks ALU_ACC_CTRL_Zero_Flag_disabled_src=1. These bounded physical comparisons do not test alternative checkpoints, training, cold full-model TT tensor-cache rebuilds, malformed full-model caches, or generic autoregressive Qwen serving.

The TT kernel binary cache used /datapool/aspen-builds/tmp/clef-next-kernels with mode 0700 and 525+ GiB free. That owner-created trial directory was removed after all meshes closed; tensor caches and retained logs were preserved, and no HOME, system or Nix file was deleted.
